result.result: The build is clean and the app is fully functional. Here's a summary of the work. ## Summary Built the full Angular 19 standalone app at `/private/tmp/dsb-eval/sonnet-5/A-prime-1` per the spec, using the arm's given design tokens (`:root` custom properties + `.tag-*` classes) verbatim as the canonical design system, and Figma data only for structural layout (grid proportions, component composition, spacing scale). **Structure**: `AuthService`/`UsersService`/`AppInMemoryDataService` in `core/`, route guards (`authGuard`/`loginGuard`), lazy-loaded `login`, `shell` (header/footer/router-outlet), `dashboard`, and `users` (table + 4 dialogs: details, edit, delete-confirm, invite) in `features/`/`layout/`. **Verified live in a browser** (Playwright driver, not just build/typecheck): login validation and wrong-credential states, successful login → dashboard, all 8 dashboard tiles, the full users CRUD round-trip (create/read/update/delete all hit the in-memory API and the table reflects changes), all four dialogs opening/closing, and auth-guard redirects (logged-out → `/login`, logged-in visiting `/login` → `/dashboard`, wildcard → `/login`, sign-out clearing session). Zero console errors throughout. **Two real bugs found and fixed during testing:** 1. The profile menu's outside-click-to-close checked containment against the entire shell's host element (which wraps the routed page too), so no click ever counted as "outside" — scoped the check to just the profile control instead. 2. `angular-in-memory-web-api`'s PUT replaces the whole record rather than patching it, so sending only `{name, email, role}` on save silently wiped `avatar`/`status`/`joinedDate` from the record — fixed by merging the full user object before the PUT. Also added a defensive initials-fallback for the avatar `` (spec requires it, even though the dicebear images happened to load fine in this sandbox). **Unverified against Figma:** the "Auth Layout"/"Main Dashboard" node's sample content (dashboard metrics, log style, service names) didn't match S0's explicit data — I followed S0's explicit values (monospace terminal-style logs, the named services, the 7-day bar chart) since it's unambiguous, and used Figma only for the structural grid/spacing/proportions.
